milestones.title: Actor support and executor architecture
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Logical cooperative-default and MainActor executor identity, source hops, caller restoration, detached-task lane identity, distinct source-actor runtime IDs, weak actor-record cleanup, canonical user-declared global-actor mapping through static shared, struct- and enum-backed arbitrary global-actor capability propagation through `#isolation` and defaulted isolated dispatch, depth-counted mailbox ownership for synchronous and async actor-function plus externally awaited synchronous computed-getter and subscript-getter segments, throwing computed-getter failure cleanup, async-throwing computed/subscript-getter success/source-error/cancellation reacquisition cleanup with caller restoration, actor computed-property and subscript-setter confinement to already-owned segments, controlled suspension release/reacquisition and actor reentrancy, task-local propagation through actor hops and suspension, retained queued actor messages after task cancellation, cross-actor throwing and cancellation-observing function hops with caller restoration, explicit plus defaulted/optional source-actor, MainActor, custom-global-actor, and nil isolated-parameter dispatch, explicit waitingForActor handoff/cleanup, replayable seeded mailbox stress with complete runtime draining, mutable stored-property confinement with Swift-compatible immutable-let and nonisolated exceptions, MainActor-owned deinitializer execution, fail-closed source-actor/user-global-actor deinitializer boundaries, and fail-closed custom actor-executor dispatch are covered.

requirements.notes: Logical cooperative-default and MainActor hops are covered without claiming physical worker execution.

The actor safety cycle is covered without a global up-front rejection. Synchronous actor initialization, task-local propagation, queued-call cancellation, actor functions, accessors, isolated parameters, mailbox ownership, storage confinement, and reentrancy use the actor runtime. The host Instance lifetime is MainActor-owned, so explicit MainActor deinitializers and isolated deinitializers on MainActor nominals execute through that real capability with exact native parity. Isolated source-actor and explicit user-global-actor teardown fail closed at first construction; ordinary and explicit nonisolated teardown remain supported. The global-actor decision resolves forward declarations and aliases. The unchanged pinned swiftlang custom_executors.swift oracle proves that a source unownedExecutor changes isolated dispatch; the interpreter classifies direct computed, direct stored, and protocol-extension-default unownedExecutor forms after nominal resolution and fails closed at isolated method/accessor/storage entry instead of substituting its mailbox. Initializers and nonisolated members remain usable, and a same-named property on a non-actor remains ordinary. Aidoku ProjectCheck proves that collecting a real stored custom-executor declaration is not rejected up front. Full custom-executor scheduling and physical threads are not claimed.

The entry slice of the 2026-07-16 demand cycle is covered. Source actor declarations retain their nominal actor kind, each instance receives a distinct runtime ID backed by a non-owning record, final release removes that record, and a collected user-declared global actor resolves through its canonical static shared identity. Synchronous and async actor-isolated functions plus externally awaited synchronous computed-property and subscript getters acquire depth-counted mailbox leases before changing logical executor; computed and subscript getters retain their declared async/throwing effects, a throwing computed getter releases the target on failure, and async-throwing computed/subscript getters reacquire their target before normal return, source-thrown error, or cancellation observation, then release it and restore their caller before subsequent caller work; computed-property and subscript setters require an already-owned actor segment because Swift rejects external mutation even when spelled with await. Canonical host/task/clock/group waits release the complete nested segment, and resumption queues on the same actor before source evaluation continues. Competing source tasks record waitingForActor, receive direct ownership handoff, and cannot release while an actor edge remains. Mutable stored-property funnels require ownership, while ordinary immutable let and explicitly nonisolated storage remain readable under the native Swift 6 rule. Exact same-source actor cases are native/interpreter GREEN in 20 repetitions without FIFO, task-start, physical-thread, or cross-actor-parallelism claims. A 64-seed replayable mailbox board varies fanout, rounds, pre-entry yield, and in-segment resume yields while proving exact mutation totals, actor ownership after every resume, complete child collection, and empty task/actor/group/scope/host-operation/scheduler registries. FoodTruckCheck, ProjectCheck, and suite ratchets must not regress.

Controlled same-source parity proves that an async actor message owns its synchronous prefix, releases the complete nested segment at a host suspension, permits a second message to mutate isolated state, and reacquires the same actor before resuming. A second exact case proves a cross-actor throwing-function hop: the callee owns its segment, releases it on error, the caller is restored before catch handling, and a later callee message retains both mutations. Gated function, async-computed-getter, and async-subscript-getter cases cancel the source task while the callee is suspended, then prove callee reacquisition before cancellation observation, balanced release, caller restoration before catch, and subsequent callee progress. A queued-call case proves that cancellation does not remove a waitingForActor edge: handoff still enters the method with actor ownership and the request remains observable. Separate source-gated async computed/subscript cases prove the same balanced target/caller transition on normal return and source-thrown error. Task-local propagation retains one task-owned binding map across actor entry, suspension, mailbox reacquisition, and dynamic-scope restoration. Isolated parameters preserve syntax metadata and select their executor from the bound runtime value before function entry. Required explicit source actors, default #isolation inherited from a source actor, MainActor, or a custom global actor, explicit source actors, explicit nil, and a nil default in nonisolated code are covered; the default is evaluated once in the caller's lexical isolation and the exact value is reused for binding. Struct- and enum-backed global-actor declarations may expose a different source-actor type as static shared; both nominal representations now preserve @globalActor metadata, resolve that exact canonical capability, and own its mailbox through nested defaulted isolated dispatch. Already-owned synchronous entry is legal, while unawaited cross-actor entry fails closed. The shared runtime path balances task, clock, host, group, accessor, and explicit executor-hop suspensions. A native-anchored exact fixture plus a 64-seed replayable stress board cover mailbox fanout, repeated rounds, suspension/reacquisition, invariant mutation totals, full child collection, and empty runtime registries without claiming FIFO or physical threads. This covers the reentrancy and isolated-dispatch slice; the per-feature actor safety boundary remains open.

milestones.title: Async sequences and continuations

Exact same-source parity covers finite success, typed source failure, cooperative user-iterator cancellation, `break`/`continue`/`return` plus per-iteration and function-level `defer` cleanup, real source and host suspension, iterator state, terminal `nil`, host-operation ownership, and registry cleanup. `AsyncStream` and `AsyncThrowingStream` share runtime-owned suspension, cancellation, finish/failure, nonnegative buffering, copied-iterator, final-owner termination, escaped non-owning producer-handle, and complete cleanup evidence. Copied throwing-stream iterators share one pending-`next()` capability per stream; overlapping calls trap, with fatal semantics preserved across gateway source-location attachment. The current `withCheckedContinuation` slice owns delayed `resume(returning:)` values, zero-argument Void `resume()`, and nonthrowing Result success through `resume(with:)` in a bounded continuation registry for explicit or caller-defaulted `nil`, `MainActor.shared`, and source-actor isolation. It records `waitingForContinuation`, runs the contextual body on the selected actor, restores a different caller executor after body return, releases an already-owned source actor while parked, permits actor reentry, reacquires that actor before continuation, distinguishes source cancellation from infrastructure abort, and drains every ownership edge. Omitted `#isolation` is materialized once in caller lexical isolation. `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` shares that record for value resume and exact source-error projection through `resume(throwing:)`; its MainActor and source-actor error paths have exact body-isolation and caller-restoration evidence, with mailbox release/reentry/reacquisition for a caller-defaulted actor, and concrete-error plus existential-error Result success/failure through `resume(with:)` delegate to those same terminal transitions. Both checked forms have process-isolated double-resume parity: the first terminal transition wins and a second resume is a fatal runtime invariant that bypasses source `do`/`catch`. Both forms also diagnose abandonment when the final unchecked source token is released: the diagnostic is a successful-process runtime warning, not a catchable error or trap, and the waiting task remains suspended until the host applies explicit teardown. A resumed token may remain escaped after owner completion without retaining the owner's task-local object, continuation record, runtime, session, or interpreter; releasing that token is inert. Task-group iteration remains separate M4 evidence. `withUnsafeContinuation` and `withUnsafeThrowingContinuation` are generated from the active SDK interface into one shared `unsupportedUnsafeContinuation` intrinsic. Apple Swift 6.3.3 accepted explicit `MainActor.shared` isolation and immediate one-shot resume as `value:33` and `value:44` in twenty bounded runs per form; the interpreter fails closed with a form-specific named unsupported-ownership diagnostic before invoking either body or allocating continuation ownership.

milestones.title: SwiftUI lifecycle
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Synchronous callbacks use runtime-owned host tasks. BridgeGen emits `.task`, `.task(id:)`, and `.refreshable`; one reusable adapter gives actual SwiftUI-owned invocations fresh `.swiftUITask` sessions. Six same-source hosting probes cover async entry, MainActor identity, disappearance cancellation, id replacement, same-id preservation, refresh trigger/completion, 32-cycle repeated teardown, and weak release of every task/session ownership object plus the final interpreter/runtime graph.
milestones.ledgerRemainingWork: The demand-scoped M8 requirement is covered. M8 remains provisional while its broad M5 and M7 dependencies remain partial; physical workers belong to active M9.

requirements.notes: Retained synchronous host callbacks enter the canonical concurrency runtime.

Gap-closure slice: before the production change, the real interpreted SwiftUI task appended only started and then failed because withTaskGroup had no canonical async runtime task; the strict native fixture returned started,value:21. BridgeGen now recognizes the three active-SDK async-closure modifier declarations and emits .task, .task(id:), and .refreshable instead of relying on the removed handwritten task gateway. Real SwiftUI retains ownership of appearance, structural identity, id replacement, and disappearance. One interface-inexpressible adapter creates a fresh parentless .swiftUITask runtime session, executes the interpreted closure through the suspending evaluator on the logical MainActor, maps native lifecycle cancellation into ordinary cooperative source cancellation, and releases the task record after completion. Six same-source NSHostingView fixtures produced stable native/interpreted observations for runtime entry, disappearance cancellation, id replacement, causal same-id task preservation, RefreshAction completion only after the async body finishes, and 32 causally sequenced appearance/removal cycles; the combined native output was identical in twenty strict Swift 6 runs with SHA-256 3c8b7ede66381a98efb6d2288c828a968c06cff1d5317c7f88796ab98d49d08b. The same-id and teardown-stress steps were already-GREEN characterizations and required no production change. The refresh spelling captured RED because the generated matcher did not apply Swift trailing-closure label relaxation to asyncAction; the shared closure-parameter rule now does so without a modifier-name branch. Each stress cycle proves a distinct task and session ID, cancellation before the next appearance, empty task/group/scope/stream/continuation/host-operation/scheduler registries, and weak release of the task record, source handle, native driver, evaluation context, and task-local storage. Removing the final host graph also releases the Interpreter and CooperativeConcurrencyRuntime; twenty fresh test processes completed 640 cycles. Measured demand (2026-07-16/17): .task appears in 30 of 669 corpus projects and four times in FoodTruck; .refreshable appears in 133 files across 32 checked-in external project trees. The demand-scoped M8 requirement is covered; M8 remains provisional only because its broad M5/M7 dependencies remain partial.

milestones.title: Optional physical parallelism
milestones.ledgerEvidence: The core remains cooperatively scheduled and main-actor hosted; no physical parallelism claim is made. ParsedProgram is immutable and Sendable and owns folded syntax, source locations, and one ParsedProgramMetadata capability containing target-neutral all-branch declaration, callable/accessor/subscript, call-site argument, member-plan, nominal, property-storage, enum-case, extension, type-alias, and deinitializer indexes. Callable facts now include immutable function bodies, names, parameters, modifiers, effects, isolation, and placement plus initializer bodies, attributes, modifiers, failable/Codable classification, and isolation facts. Call-site facts include labels/expressions, first and additional trailing-closure structure, and bare unqualified direct-reference spelling while compiler predicates are excluded. Synchronous/suspending argument collection and bounded async-operation provenance consume those immutable facts; overload resolution and call-target identity remain session-owned. Member plans classify every direct nominal/extension declaration and nested conditional clause; each session resolves one active member sequence before mutable symbol materialization. Runtime function body/shape/placement dispatch, initializer selection/execution, nominal/member/storage/case materialization, extension target/conformance handling, alias binding, and deinitializer body/isolation-policy attachment consume immutable metadata while mutable runtime symbols, values, and materialized members remain MainActor-confined. Each session resolves one build-specific top-level plan before mutable runtime-symbol materialization. Each Interpreter owns a distinct MainActor-confined RuntimeHeap. Every runAsync program entry executes through a single-use InterpreterSession, and program roots, callbacks, SwiftUI tasks, and their source tasks carry an explicit RuntimeEntry preserving the originating metadata snapshot. Causally controlled native parity proves callback overlap, while conditional-member, explicit-nil task-executor-preference, `extractIsolation`, actor-subscript, custom-global-actor, actor-initialization, enum-case, extension, type-alias, ordinary-deinitializer, callable-placement, and initializer-declaration parity characterize or close metadata semantics. The source-callable _swift_createJobForTestingOnly hook remains preflight-only/deferred. Each InterpreterSession owns one immutable target-specific ResolvedProgramPlan containing its file identity and SourceLocationConverter, and its RuntimeEntry plus escaped source closures retain that exact source map and top-level/member selection across host callbacks, SwiftUI tasks, and source tasks. Exact same-source parity proves lexical `#line` provenance survives suspension. Each prepared program also owns one MainActor-confined RuntimeProgramState containing its mutable declaration/symbol registries; the session, entries, and escaped closures retain that exact state across the same boundaries instead of consulting the facade's latest program. CooperativeConcurrencyRuntime now strongly owns session-scheduled unstructured and detached task handles until autonomous completion or session-policy release; Interpreter exposes only a read-only compatibility inspection view. The runtime also allocates every asynchronous EvaluationTaskContext identity through one factory; only the facade's synchronous compatibility context retains reserved ID 0. EvaluationTaskContext identifies that owning runtime through a weak capability instead of retaining or identifying an Interpreter facade; explicit TaskBoundEvalContext host re-entry ownership remains separate. Native-stack guard geometry is likewise EvaluationTaskContext-owned, keyed to the numeric ID of its supplying pthread, refreshed after migration, and cleared with task dynamic state.
milestones.ledgerRemainingWork: Complete immutable indexing for remaining member semantics and compiler-only signature families, call-site semantic resolution, and compiler-preflight metadata, finish moving mutable runtime-symbol materialization and evaluation behind InterpreterSession, classify every heap edge for worker access, add physical-worker scheduling, Thread Sanitizer evidence, and cooperative-versus-parallel semantic parity without exposing Box, Environment, or Instance to races.

requirements.notes: Twenty-eight M9 prerequisite slices are green. ResolvedProgramPlan, RuntimeProgramState, and RuntimeEntry preserve exact target, source, mutable-symbol, HostRegistry, task-handle, evaluator-context, and native-stack-guard provenance across sessions, callbacks, descendant tasks, and SwiftUI tasks. The twenty-seventh RED proved an origin callback could be redirected to a newer HostRegistry; binding the registry to RuntimeProgramState restored origin while a newly prepared program returned newer. The twenty-eighth RED proved the remaining process-wide Date.now provider could likewise be cleared by a newer program: an escaped origin callback returned the wall-clock day instead of its frozen day. Host coercions now request a type/member-parameterized sourceStaticMember capability from their bound EvalContext, which resolves through the exact runtime entry; non-interpreter contexts return nil. A standalone Apple Swift 6.3.3 probe passed implicit .now into Calendar.startOfDay(for:) after Task.yield() and returned exact 1784160000 with a UTC calendar in three runs. The host-static-shadow-after-suspension fixture returns exact 1784228400 in twenty native/interpreter repetitions, with every native shard reporting SHA-256 49bde28776cde22ce6aa47e119d3ecbb34246309ef8fa2bddb609146a19e692c. Focused tests retain FoodTruck Calendar coercion, qualified/annotated static shadowing, source-map/registry/static-member callback provenance, and real SwiftUI task entry. The canonical parallel iteration completed seven targeted tests in four suites, all forty-two methodology checks, and all twenty exact parity repetitions on four workers in 1.8 seconds. Scheduler order, physical threads, Sendable host bridges, and physical parallelism are not claimed. Each Interpreter still owns one MainActor-confined RuntimeHeap shared by its sessions; active evaluation and explicit host re-entry use the facade while mutable symbol/value graphs and HostRegistry implementations remain confined. Remaining member semantics, call-site semantic resolution, compiler metadata indexing, completion of mutable-symbol/evaluator migration, worker-safe heap classification, physical workers, ExecutorJob creation/scheduling, Thread Sanitizer, and parity between cooperative and parallel modes remain unimplemented.
